evals.name: quantstart-ou-url-to-markdown
evals.prompt: Convert https://www.quantstart.com/articles/ornstein-uhlenbeck-simulation-with-python into a markdown file I can feed to my AI agents later. The math and the Python code need to survive — last converter I tried lost all the equations.
evals.expected_output: A markdown file of the OU article with front-matter provenance, native $$...$$ LaTeX for the SDE and its solution, inline $X_t$-style math, language-tagged Python fences (including the Full Code listing), the simulation plot downloaded to media/, and no site chrome.
expectations: A markdown file exists in the outputs directory with substantial content (at least 4000 characters)
YAML front matter is present with source: https://www.quantstart.com/articles/ornstein-uhlenbeck-simulation-with-python and a title that does NOT carry a '| QuantStart' suffix
Display math survived: the SDE appears inside $$ delimiters as LaTeX (contains \theta (\mu - X_t) dt + \sigma dW_t), with no \begin{eqnarray} left outside $$ blocks
Inline math survived: at least 20 $...$ spans such as $X_t$, $\mu$, $\theta$, and none of the broken-sentence symptoms ('at time , is the long-term mean' with the symbol missing)
The Python simulation appears as a fenced ```python block containing np.random.normal, including the final 'Full Code' listing
The simulation plot is referenced from the markdown either as a downloaded media/ file or as an absolute image URL (not silently dropped)
No site chrome leaked into the output: no 'Quantcademy', no cookie/subscribe/advert boilerplate
No unconverted \( or \[ markers outside code fences and no leftover ZQ...MQZ... placeholder tokens

evals.name: quantstart-bayesian-regression-url-to-markdown
evals.prompt: Please save https://www.quantstart.com/articles/batch-linear-regression-via-bayesian-estimation as markdown for offline reading by agents. It's equation-dense so I want the formulas intact and the code listings runnable.
evals.expected_output: A markdown file of the Bayesian batch linear regression article with $$...$$ display equations (posterior/product formulas), $\theta$-style inline math, five ```python fences, and clean front matter.
expectations: A markdown file exists in the outputs directory with substantial content (at least 6000 characters)
Front matter title is 'Batch Linear Regression via Bayesian Estimation' with the canonical source URL
Equation-dense math survived: at least 10 $$...$$ display blocks including a \prod_{k=1}^T formula, and inline math such as $\theta$, $y_k$, $\sigma^2$
All five Python code listings appear as ```python fenced blocks (including one with a __main__ entrypoint), with no <span class= highlighter junk inside fences
Math variable references in prose survived: '\$k\$-th' style mangling does NOT occur (the phrase reads '$k$-th' or similar), and '$n=50$' stays as math rather than escaped currency
The book citation link (Särkkä / Bayesian Filtering and Smoothing) is preserved with an absolute URL
No raw \begin{eqnarray} outside $$ blocks and no unbalanced $ delimiter lines flagged by a manual skim

evals.name: offline-fixture-html-with-chrome-and-currency
evals.prompt: I saved a copy of a blog article at skills/convert-web-article-to-md/evals/fixtures/quantstart-style-article.html — turn it into a clean markdown file in the outputs directory, keeping the math and code.
evals.expected_output: A markdown file converted from the local fixture: loose \begin{eqnarray} blocks become $$ math, inline \( \) becomes $ math, the Prism block becomes a ```python fence with entities unescaped, prose currency stays escaped, and nav/cookie/advert/subscribe/footer chrome is gone.
expectations: A markdown file exists in the outputs directory with at least 1200 characters of body content
Both loose \begin{eqnarray} equations appear inside $$...$$ (containing dS_t = \theta (\mu - S_t) dt + \sigma dW_t), with no raw \begin{eqnarray} remaining
Inline math converted: $S_t$, $\Delta t$, $N$ appear as $...$ spans, not as \$S\$-style escaped currency
Prose currency is escaped so it cannot pair into math: the text contains \$5,000 and \$10,000
The Python block is a ```python fence whose content includes 'np.random.normal' and unescaped comparison operators (e.g. '<' rather than '<')
Chrome is stripped: no 'Subscribe', 'cookie', 'Related Posts', or site-footer text anywhere in the markdown; the advert image (sidebar-advert) is absent
Front matter includes author 'Fixture Author', published date 2026-08-14, and the canonical quantblog.example URL
